My office is happy to report that my amendment to remove pesticide liability protections will receive a vote on the House floor as part of the Farm Bill. 

However, the Rules Committee is currently packaging the Farm Bill together with FISA and reconciliation under a single rule.

If you commit fraud in Minnesota you’re going to get caught — and that’s exactly what we saw today. We catch criminals when state and federal agencies share information. Joint investig

This week, Congress is supposed to vote on:

1. FISA
2. The Farm Bill
3. Reconciliation

So why does anyone think it’s a good idea to bundle three wildly different pieces of legislation into a single rule?

How did we get to a point where China controls such a significant share of U.S. pork production? 

And why is Congress voting on legislation that would help China expand that hold instead of squash it?
The rule on all three of these bills (FISA, Farm Bill, etc.) should be separate. It’s a mistake to lump them together.
The data is clear, the priority should be too. Why is Congress voting to protect pesticides over people?

China already controls a massive share of U.S. pork production, and the “Save Our Bacon Act” only strengthens that grip. 

I’m leading Amendment #28 to remove Save Our Bacon because overturning state laws doesn’t just hurt farmers, it risks further consolidating our food system in the hands of global corporations, including those tied to China.

I’m proud to lead Amendment #28 to strike the so-called “Save Our Bacon Act.” It’s not just about farming, it’s about national security. This bill risks handing more control of our food supply to foreign adversaries like China. 

I will always stand with American farmers over foreign-owned interests.

This week, the Farm Bill is being debated in Congress while the Supreme Court is simultaneously hearing oral arguments in the Bayer/Roundup case, which is one of the most consequential pesticide liability cases in American history. 

For Congress to strip states of their ability to set stricter pesticide standards at this exact moment, before the Supreme Court has even weighed in, would be reckless to say the least.

Moms across this country are paying attention. To tackle the chronic disease crisis, we need proactive prevention that targets root causes, not reactionary treatment after it’s already too late. 

We want a healthier future for our kids. Casey Means represents that shift. Moms, families, and patients are watching: Confirm her @SenateGOP @CaseyMeansMD
